doc_name: Bruno Kreisky Prize for Services to Human Rights
text: The Bruno Kreisky Prize for Human Rights is a biennial award established in October 1976 to mark the 65th birthday of Bruno Kreisky. It recognizes individuals and organizations for their significant contributions to human rights. In 1993, the prize was split into two components: a human rights prize, awarded between 7,000 and 30,000 Euros, and a prize for merit. The Bruno Kreisky Foundation for Human Rights has presented the award in 14 conferments, honoring more than 130 individuals, institutions, and human rights projects for exceptional service in advancing and protecting international human rights and for outstanding achievements in humanitarian aid. The selection of prize winners is carried out jointly by the board of trustees of the Bruno Kreisky Foundation and an international jury.
